add_transaction.description: Sends any transaction add -- an invoice, a bill, a sales receipt, a check, a journal entry -- once every list record it names exists. QuickBooks refuses the whole add for one missing customer, item, class or terms, so the distinct references the add makes (the same item on five lines is one) are made sure of first, in two passes. The first only finds, and asks: resolve looks for each by its ListID or its name, matched by rank on a realtime connection (with the fields and accept your app sent beside its add), and your app picks among near matches; an account, sales tax code, terms, price level or sales tax item that isn't there, or any record your app sent no add for, is your app's to pick from the active ones. A cancel there ends the run with nothing created. The second creates what the first didn't find -- a stale ListID included: a customer, vendor or item from the add your app sent for it in `adds`, a class, payment method, ship method or customer message from its name alone, through ensure, which asks your app when the name is held elsewhere; a cancel there stops the rest. `references` changes those rules per kind. Then the add goes out with every reference replaced by its ListID. The output's `record` is the transaction, lines included, and its `references` say, for every place the add names a record, keyed by that place in the params your app sent (`customer_ref`, `invoice_line_add.0.item_ref`), how it ended and the record used. If QuickBooks never answers the add, the run settles it before this chart hears of it, by the GUID the add carries: it is found rather than added twice, read with its lines, and your app is asked only when looking cannot tell, told why.

pull_changes.description: The sync: every record of the kinds your app names that QuickBooks changed on or after `since`, handed to your app a page at a time, then the ones deleted since then; without `since`, every record of those kinds and no deletions, the initial import. Each kind runs stream_query, so the pages arrive as its `page` notifications with `kind` the word you gave; with `since`, the deletions arrive last, as one `deleted` notification; and workflow_run.completed says how many of each there were. Start it with a webhook_url, and keep the time you started it as the next run's `since`, so a change made while this one runs is sent again rather than missed. QuickBooks keeps deletions for 90 days, so a `since` older than that misses some; run it without `since` to start over instead. A kind QuickBooks refuses stops the run: the pages already sent were sent, and a run started again sends them again, so take a repeated page without harm.

include_line_items.description: true sends each transaction with its lines (invoice_line_ret and the like), so your app need not read them one by one. Four kinds take no such parameter -- build_assembly, charge, time_tracking and vehicle_mileage -- and fail at their start when it is on: leave them out of transactions, or pull them in a run of their own. Left out or false, each record is the header, and your app reads one whole by its txn_id when it needs the lines.

lists.description: The lists to pull, as kind words that name both the list's query and its deleted-records type: customer, vendor, account, class, employee, other_name, the item kinds (item_service, item_non_inventory, item_inventory, item_inventory_assembly, item_other_charge, item_discount, item_subtotal, item_payment, item_sales_tax, item_sales_tax_group, item_group, item_fixed_asset) and every other type a ListDeleted query takes, all but billing_rate, whose query has no active-status filter. Inactive records are included. QuickBooks pages only customers, vendors and items; every other list answers whole and arrives as one page, however long. Send [] to pull only transactions.

since.description: When your app last synced, as a date and time QuickBooks reads as on or after, in the company file's local time unless it carries an offset: 2026-10-01T00:00:00, or 2026-10-01T00:00:00-05:00. Records modified, and records deleted, from then on are sent. Left out, every record of the kinds named is sent, active or not, and no deletions: the first sync.

transactions.description: The transactions to pull, as kind words that name both the transaction's query and its deleted-records type: invoice, receive_payment, sales_receipt, credit_memo, estimate, sales_order, bill, bill_payment_check, check, credit_card_charge, deposit, journal_entry, purchase_order, vendor_credit and the rest of the types a TxnDeleted query takes. Each record is the transaction's header, without its lines, unless include_line_items is true.

push_records.description: A bulk push: up to 200 list records your app holds, each made to exist in QuickBooks with its fields by upsert -- found by the ListID your app stored or by its name, matched by rank on a realtime connection, and updated, or added when nothing is the record -- one at a time, in order, in one run. A record QuickBooks refuses does not stop the rest: its error is listed and the next one goes. A record whose name only has near matches, or whose QuickBooks record someone changed after the run read it, pauses the run with upsert's question, which your app answers on this run; `prompt.from.item_index` says which record asks. The output lists what happened to each, in the order sent. For a webhook per record, start one upsert run per record instead.

A record with a field upsert doesn't take, or a field of the wrong type, refuses the run before anything is sent; otherwise each is checked when its turn comes, so one upsert refuses is listed among the errors and the rest still go. Records of different lists may be mixed.

record_payment.description: Records a customer's payment and applies it to one invoice, found the way resolve_transaction does: by the TxnID your app stored, by its number, or among the invoices your filters select, with the external_guid your app kept telling look-alikes apart. The invoice's own customer receives the payment, and the amount defaults to what the invoice still owes, so the common case needs only the invoice and how it was paid. An invoice already paid in full is reported rather than paid twice; an amount over the balance is QuickBooks' to refuse, in its own words.

external_guid.description: The GUID the add was sent with, as the workflow that added it reported in ref.external_guid: tells the transaction apart from look-alikes.

filters.description: The invoice query's own filters (invoice.query's params), for when there is no id or number to go by: {"entity_filter": {"full_name": ["Acme"]}, "txn_date_range_filter": {"from_txn_date": "2026-10-01", "to_txn_date": "2026-10-31"}}, say. Left out, a lookup without an id or a number has nothing to go by and ends not_found.

payment.description: How it was paid: payment_method_ref, deposit_to_account_ref, ref_number (a check number), txn_date, memo -- and total_amount only when it is not the whole balance. customer_ref and applied_to_txn_add are filled in from the invoice.

ref_number.description: The reference number, such as an invoice number: tried when there is no id, or the id is stale.

txn_id.description: The TxnID your app stored, if any: tried first.

record_payment.name: Record a payment against an invoice

resolve.description: Turns what your app holds about a list record -- a customer, vendor, employee or other name, an item, an account, a class, terms or any other list a transaction names -- into that record, read whole. The ListID your app stored goes first; then the name is matched: ranked against the connection's name index on a realtime or simulated connection, so `ACME, Inc.` finds `Acme Inc`, or through QuickBooks' own filters on a standard one. Only an exact match is used without asking (or a strong one, with accept: strong); near matches are your app's to pick from, and when too many are alike it is asked for a detail that tells them apart instead. Jobs and sub-items are found under their parent, given by full name or ListID. It only finds, and asks: with pick, a record that isn't there is your app's to pick from the active ones instead. ensure creates what is missing, and upsert brings what it finds up to date.

accept.description: exact (the default): only a record with exactly that name is used without asking. strong: a single strong match is used too -- the same name apart from punctuation, suffixes, word order or spacing, or the same account number. Acme Inc and Acme LLC are a strong match and can be two companies, so ask for strong only when that can't happen in your data.

fields.description: For customer, vendor, employee, other_name and entity: what else your app knows, matched as well as the name -- company_name, email, phone, account_number, city, postal_code (an employee has no company_name). The same account number is a strong match on its own; the same email, phone or postal code makes a similar name a strong one.

kind.description: Which list: customer, vendor, employee, other_name, entity (those four together, one name space), item (every item type) or one item type such as item_service, account, class, standard_terms, date_driven_terms, terms, sales_tax_code, payment_method, ship_method, price_level, customer_type, vendor_type, job_type, sales_rep or customer_msg, or another list a transaction names, such as inventory_site or currency. Every kind but the last few is matched by rank on a realtime connection; those are looked up by their exact full name only.

list_id.description: The ListID your app stored for the record, if any. Tried first: a ListID survives a rename. A stale one (the record was merged or deleted) falls through to the name.

name.description: The record's own name, without its parent's: Kitchen for the job Smith:Kitchen. Required unless list_id is sent.

parent.description: For a job or a sub-item (or a subaccount, a subclass): its parent, by full name or ListID. Only that parent's children are considered.

pick.description: true: when nothing is like the name, or your app says none of the near matches is it, your app is asked to pick one of the kind's active records (the first 50) instead of the run ending not_found. For a record nothing may be created for: ensure without an add, and add_transaction's accounts, sales tax codes and terms use it.

resolve.name: Resolve a list record (any kind)

resolve_transaction.description: Turns what your app holds about a transaction into that transaction, surest first: the TxnID it stored; then the reference number, which answers with every transaction so numbered; then the filters your query carries, such as the customer and a date range. Among several, the one carrying the external_guid your app kept from the add is it; with no GUID to go by, one transaction with the number is it, and anything less sure is offered to your app to pick from. It only finds, and without line items: read the record whole by its txn_id when you need the lines. Generic over the transaction type, because the query arrives as input.

external_guid.description: The GUID the add was sent with, as the workflow that added it reported in ref.external_guid, written as QuickBooks writes it: braces and upper case. Among several transactions, the one carrying it is the one added.

query.description: The transaction query, such as {"operation": "invoice.query", "params": {}}. Its params are the filters that narrow the lookup when there is no number to go by: an entity_filter, a txn_date_range_filter. Leave txn_id, ref_number and max_returned out; the chart sets them.

operation.description: The operation to send: any the API offers.

params.description: Its parameters, as the v2 endpoint for that operation takes them.

ref_number.description: The reference number, such as an invoice number. QuickBooks does not keep numbers unique, so the lookup answers with every transaction so numbered, and external_guid tells them apart.

txn_id.description: The TxnID your app stored, if any. Tried first; one QuickBooks no longer knows (the transaction was deleted) falls through to the number or the filters.

resolve_transaction.name: Resolve a transaction (any type)

stream_query.description: Hands your app every record a query finds, a page at a time, as `page` notifications, then how many there were. Generic over the query, because it arrives as input: every customer, the items changed since a date, one customer's invoices -- whatever the query's own filters select, for any query. Start it with a webhook_url: each page is a workflow_run.notification webhook, and the run waits for your app's 2xx before fetching the next, so pages arrive in order and all of them before workflow_run.completed. QuickBooks keeps the pages only for the Web Connector session that fetched the first; if that session ends part way, the run starts again from page 1, at most three passes, so your app should take a page it has already seen without harm. A `pass` above 1 on a page says it may be one.

kind.description: A word for your app to route the pages on, sent as `kind` in every notification and in the output: customers, say. Left out, it is the query's operation id, such as customer.query.

query.description: The query to page through, such as {"operation": "customer.query", "params": {"active_status": "All"}}, or one with from_modified_date for the records changed since your app last asked. Leave max_returned and iterator out: the chart pages 200 at a time. A query for one record by its id or full name has no pages; page through what filters find instead. A query QuickBooks does not page -- account.query and the other short lists, list_deleted.query and txn_deleted.query, the company, preferences and host queries, the reports -- answers whole and arrives as one page, however many records it holds. Anything but a query fails the run before it is sent.

operation.description: The operation to send: any the API offers.

params.description: Its parameters, as the v2 endpoint for that operation takes them.

stream_query.name: Stream a query to the app

upsert.description: Makes a QuickBooks list record exist with the fields your app holds. Finds it the way resolve does -- the ListID your app stored, then the name, matched by rank on a realtime connection, with near matches for your app to pick from -- and sends the update you pass to whichever record that turns up, even when its fields already match. When nothing is the record it sends the add you pass instead. resolve only finds; this is the chart that writes. The update leaves edit_sequence out: the engine reads the record first, and if someone changed it after that read the run asks your app before anything is overwritten.

add.description: The add to send when nothing is the record, exactly as the v2 <kind>.create endpoint takes it, carrying every field the record should have: a created record is not updated as well. Its name, and its parent_ref for a job or a sub-item, are what is looked for. If the name is taken between the lookup and the add (3100), the lookup runs once more.

update.description: The fields to set on the record once it is found or picked, as the v2 <list>.update endpoint takes them: {"phone": "512-555-0100"}. Leave list_id and edit_sequence out: the chart fills in the ListID of the record it found, and the engine reads the edit sequence before sending. A field left out keeps its value in QuickBooks.

void_transaction.description: Voids a transaction -- or deletes it, when you say so -- after finding it the way resolve_transaction does: by the TxnID your app stored, by its number, or among the transactions your filters select, with the external_guid your app kept telling look-alikes apart. Voiding keeps the record with its amounts at zero, which is what the books usually want; deleting removes it for good. Generic over the transaction type through `kind`: QuickBooks voids sixteen types (invoice, bill, check, journal_entry and the others `kind` lists) and deletes those and nine more (sales_order, estimate, purchase_order, receive_payment, time_tracking and four others), so a kind that cannot be voided is deleted with `action` delete, and asking to void one fails at once, before anything is looked up or sent. A transaction your app cannot identify is offered to it to pick from, and nothing is voided or deleted until it does.

kind.description: The transaction type, as the operation ids name it. To void (the default), one of the sixteen types a TxnVoid request takes: ar_refund_credit_card, bill, bill_payment_check, bill_payment_credit_card, charge, check, credit_card_charge, credit_card_credit, credit_memo, deposit, inventory_adjustment, invoice, item_receipt, journal_entry, sales_receipt, vendor_credit. To delete (`action` delete), those and the nine more a TxnDel request takes: build_assembly, estimate, purchase_order, receive_payment, sales_order, sales_tax_payment_check, time_tracking, transfer_inventory, vehicle_mileage. Asking to void one of those nine fails at once and nothing is sent; deposit, time_tracking and vehicle_mileage have no reference number, so find them by txn_id or filters.
